newsitem.title: USA: Concorde Gaming agrees to end casino pact.
newsitem.headline: Concorde Gaming agrees to end casino pact.

text.p: Concorde Gaming Corp said its Bruce H. Lien Co subsidiary and three affiliated Native American tribes agreed to terminate a management contract for the 4 Bears Casino & Lodge to resolve disputes.
The agreement provides for the termination of the contract pending an $8.65 million payment by the tribes by April 30, 1997, Concorde said in a release issued September 30.
The agreement also requires the dismissal of all litigation between the parties on the closing date.

After receiving the $8.65 million payment, Concorde said it will relinquish control of the 4 Bears Casino & Lodge, located on the Fort Berthold Reservation, near New Town, N.D. The company will continue to manage the 4 Bears Casino & Lodge and receive monthly distributions payment is made in full.
Concorde said the pact is contingent upon the tribes obtaining financing, and may be subject to approval by the National Indian Gaming Commission and/or the Secretary of the Interior.
Concorde said the pact eliminates legal uncertainty surrounding it since proceedings began almost two years ago.

"More importantly, a successful closing of this agreement will provide approximately $5 million of available capital, after repayment of certain debts related to the management agreement, which will enable the company to actively pursue other gaming opportunities," Jerry Baum, president, said.

The company said it recently presented to the Missouri Gaming Commission its market-share analysis of its proposed riverboat project in Lexington, Mo. It was among nine companies to present to the commission.
If licensed, the company will proceed with developing an estimated $17 million riverboat project in Lexington.
